repos_read.what_it_does: ETH vs BTC relative-strength signal: difference of two ATR-normalised close-minus-MA indicators, traded on ETH hourly
Normalised permutation entropy indicator (order 3, 168-pattern window) on BTC hourly close and volume; no trading rule
PCA of RSI(2..24), linear model of the next 6-bar return, walk-forward long/short on the extreme 1% prediction tails
Rule-coded chart patterns (harmonics, head and shoulders, flags, pennants), market-profile support/resistance, PIP shape miner with k-means, plus swing detectors
Natural visibility graph of the last 12 closes; long/short from average shortest path length of price vs negated price; unfinished forecast function
Gradient-descent fit of tightest support and resistance trendlines; plots slopes only, no trading rule. Same code is repeated inside two other repos
Trendline breakout long trades with ATR take-profit/stop, then a walk-forward random forest meta-label that filters which breakouts to take
Hawkes-process smoothing of ATR-normalised candle range; trades the direction of the move when volatility spikes after a quiet spell
Non-repainting ATR zigzag swing detector with hierarchical swing levels; engine only, no strategy
Monte Carlo permutation test toolkit: bar_permute (single and multi-market), in-sample and walk-forward permutation tests on a Donchian breakout and a decision tree

ideas.name: RSI-PCA walk-forward return predictor
ideas.markets: BTCUSDT hourly close only (BTCUSDT3600.csv). The in-sample file uses data before 2020-01-01; the walk-forward is scored from 2020 onward
ideas.entry: Wilder RSI (pandas_ta) for every period 2..24 (23 features), centred by the training-window mean, projected on the first 3 eigenvectors of their covariance, then least squares (no intercept) onto the next-6-bar log return. Long signal when the prediction exceeds the 99th percentile of the training window's own predictions, short signal below the 1st percentile. The position is the 6-bar rolling mean of the raw +1/-1/0 signal, so every signal is held 6 bars and overlapping signals stack into a fractional position
ideas.exit: No explicit exit: each signal drops out of the rolling mean after 6 bars
ideas.parameters: RSI periods 2..24; n_components 3; lookahead 6; rolling train window 2 years of bars (24*365*2); retrain every 1 year of bars; tail thresholds 1% and 99%. Nothing is optimised in the main run, but a commented heatmap sweeps lookahead 1..24 x components 1..6 on the walk-forward profit factor, and the 3 and 6 used look picked from it
ideas.claimed_results: none (README only links a video; the plot label says 'RSI-PSA 3-6 Model')
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Partial: built on RSI like the RSI(5) tests, but a multi-period model rather than a threshold rule. Not tested before
ideas.red_flags: Eigenvector bug: scipy eigh returns eigenvectors as columns, but the code uses evecs[j], a row, at RSI-PCA.txt lines 39, 114, 189 and 241, so the 'principal components' are not the real PCs (still a rotation applied consistently, so not look-ahead). No look-ahead otherwise: walkforward.py line 232 drops the last 6 training rows so every label is known at the fit date. Fills at the signal bar's close (return close i to i+1), no costs. 6-bar targets overlap heavily so the effective sample is small. On daily bars a 2-year window puts only about 5 points in each 1% tail, so train much longer (8+ years on ETFs)
ideas.why_priority: Builds on the only edge that survived (RSI dip-buying), has complete walk-forward code, and asks whether a multi-period RSI model beats the single RSI(5) rule

ideas.name: ETH minus BTC relative-strength difference (CMMA)
ideas.markets: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT hourly OHLC; BTC is the signal source, only ETH is traded
ideas.entry: cmma(x) = (close - SMA(24)) / (ATR(168) * sqrt(24)), ATR from pandas_ta on raw high/low/close, for both ETH and BTC. diff = cmma_ETH - cmma_BTC. Position in ETH only: long when diff goes above +0.25, short when it goes below -0.25
ideas.exit: Flat when diff returns to 0 or lower (long) or 0 or higher (short). No stop, no time stop
ideas.parameters: lookback 24, threshold 0.25, ATR lookback 168. Commented grid: lookback 6..72 step 3 x threshold 0.05..0.5 (19 values), scored by profit factor over the whole sample with no out-of-sample
ideas.claimed_results: none (README is empty; the script prints profit factor and per-side win rates only)
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: signal at bar i, return close i to i+1 (intermarket.py lines 104 and 119 in IntramarketDifference.txt). The function is called threshold_revert_signal but entry is momentum in relative strength (long the asset that is outperforming); only the exit is a reversion to zero. The grid is in-sample. The ETH leg is unhedged so crypto beta is in the returns. No costs. One pair on daily ETH-USD (starts late 2017, about 3,000 bars) is a small sample: test with the joint permutation of both series, and also run the rule on ETF pairs (sector ETF vs SPY) which have far more history. Lookbacks need rescaling for daily bars
ideas.why_priority: Complete rules and a cross-asset idea we have not tested, cheap on daily bars, and it forces us to build the joint-permutation test

ideas.name: Hawkes volatility compression-then-spike breakout
ideas.entry: norm_range = (ln high - ln low) / ATR(336), ATR computed on log high/low/close. Hawkes series h[t] = kappa * (h[t-1]*exp(-kappa) + norm_range[t]), kappa applied to the whole series at the end. Rolling 5th and 95th percentile of h over 168 bars (current bar included). last_below = most recent bar where h < q05. Entry on the bar where h crosses above q95 (h[t] > q95[t] and h[t-1] <= q95[t-1]) once a last_below exists: long if close[t] > close[last_below], else short
ideas.exit: Flat on the first bar where h < q05 again. No stop, no time stop; the position persists otherwise
ideas.parameters: kappa 0.1, norm ATR lookback 336, quantile lookback 168, quantiles 0.05 and 0.95. Commented grid: kappa [0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01] x quantile lookback [24, 48, 96, 168, 336] by profit factor, in-sample
ideas.claimed_results: none (README links a video; the script prints profit factor, win rates, average trade and time in market)
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: signal at close i, return close i to i+1 (hawkes.py line 132 in VolatilityHawkes.txt). The 5x5 grid is in-sample with no permutation test, so the 0.1/168 choice carries selection bias. Same-bar close fill, no costs. On daily bars the same bar counts mean a 336-day ATR and 168-day quantile window; trade count per market will be small, so run it on the 28-ETF set plus BTC and ETH
ideas.why_priority: Complete, look-ahead-free rules for a volatility regime idea that none of our current tests cover

ideas.name: Visibility-graph average path length long/short
ideas.entry: Take the last 12 raw closes (window ends at the current bar). Build a natural visibility graph of the window and of the negated window (ts2vg NaturalVG), compute the average shortest path length of each (networkx). Long (+1) if the price graph's path length is greater than the negated graph's, short (-1) if smaller, flat on a tie
ideas.exit: The position is re-decided every bar; no separate exit
ideas.parameters: lookback 12; commented heatmap lookback 6..24 by long, short and combined profit factor, in-sample. The graph is built on raw prices, not log prices, and visibility is not invariant to that choice
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: window ends at bar i, return is close i to i+1 (network_indicators.py lines 195 and 204). Odd mechanism with a 6..24 lookback sweep in-sample, so a pass needs a permutation test over the whole sweep. A 12-point visibility graph is trivial to write in numpy, so ts2vg and networkx are not required. Same-bar close fill
ideas.why_priority: One-line rule on a 12-bar window, almost free to run on 28 ETFs; the mechanism is odd so expect a null but it costs little

ideas.name: Market-profile support/resistance penetration
ideas.entry: Each bar: take the last 365 log closes (current included), fit a gaussian KDE (equal weights since first_w=1.0), evaluate on a 200-step grid between the window min and max, keep peaks whose prominence is at least 25% of the highest density as price levels. Long when close[t] > level and close[t-1] <= level; short when close[t] < level and close[t-1] >= level. If several levels cross on one bar the last in the list wins
ideas.exit: Reverse on the opposite cross; always in the market after the first signal. No stop
ideas.parameters: lookback 365, first_w 1.0, atr_mult 3.0, prominence threshold 0.25, KDE bandwidth factor = ATR(365, log) * 3. Nothing optimised in the code
ideas.claimed_results: none (the main block computes returns and trade lists but prints no statistics; comment calls it a trend following strategy)
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none directly; it is a trend-following signal, related in family to P-0084
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: levels at bar i use closes up to bar i and the cross test compares close[i-1] with close[i] (mp_support_resist.py, TechnicalAnalysisAutomation.txt lines 1538-1565). The current close feeds the KDE that defines the level it then crosses. A scalar bw_method in scipy's gaussian_kde scales the window's standard deviation (line 1506), so kernel width is not ATR x 3 as the comment implies. No author results to compare against. Same-bar close fill. One KDE per bar makes permutation tests slow, so budget permutations
ideas.why_priority: Written on daily bars already so it runs as is on BTC, ETH and our ETFs with no rescaling, and the rules are complete

ideas.name: Trendline breakout long/short (always in market)
ideas.markets: BTCUSDT hourly close (raw closes in trendline_breakout.py; log closes in the dataset and walk-forward files)
ideas.entry: Each bar, take the previous 72 closes (current bar excluded), fit an OLS line, then slide the slope by gradient search until it is the tightest line with every window close on one side: the resistance line pivots on the highest residual, the support line on the lowest. Project both to the current bar. Long if close > projected resistance, short if close < projected support
ideas.exit: Reverse on the opposite break; otherwise hold the previous signal
ideas.parameters: lookback 72; commented sweep 24..168 step 2 by profit factor, in-sample
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: P-0084 100-day breakout (same family: breakout of a prior-range boundary)
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: the window excludes the current bar and the line is projected to it (trendline_breakout.py, TrendlineBreakoutMetaLabel.txt lines 400-418). Raw vs log price is inconsistent across files. The in-sample sweep has no permutation test. The pure-Python slope optimiser is slow per bar. Same-bar close fill
ideas.why_priority: Same family as the 100-day breakout already running in P-0084, so little new information for the effort

ideas.name: Trendline breakout with ATR barriers and random-forest meta-label
ideas.markets: BTCUSDT hourly OHLCV; scored from 2020 onward
ideas.entry: Resistance trendline on the previous 72 log closes as in D-06. Long at the close when close[t] > projected resistance and no trade is open. Features at entry: resistance slope / ATR, mean gap between line and window / ATR, max gap / ATR, volume / rolling 168-bar median volume, ADX(72). Label = trade return > 0. Walk-forward: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_depth=3, random_state=69420) trained on trades that both entered and exited inside the 2-year training window, retrained yearly; the trade is taken only if predicted probability > 0.5
ideas.exit: Take profit at entry + 3 ATR(168, log), stop at entry - 3 ATR, or 12 bars, checked on closes
ideas.parameters: lookback 72, hold 12, TP and SL multiples 3.0 and 3.0, ATR lookback 168, train 24*365*2, step 24*365, probability threshold 0.5. Nothing is optimised in the code
ideas.claimed_results: none (the script prints profit factor, average trade, win rate and time in market for all trades vs meta-labelled trades)
ideas.data_needed_if_not: Trade count is the limit: daily bars give far fewer entries than 8 years of hourly, so pool across the 28 ETFs with the ATR-normalised features
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Entry rule is in the P-0084 breakout family; the meta-label layer is new
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: training uses only trades with exit_i before the fit bar (walkforward.py line 519 in TrendlineBreakoutMetaLabel.txt) and features use bars up to the entry close. Long-only on a bull-heavy BTC sample; the repo compares against buy and hold but has no permutation test on the meta-labelled result. Same-bar close fill
ideas.why_priority: Meta-labelling is worth copying as a method, but this breakout rule yields few daily trades and overlaps P-0084

ideas.name: Walk-forward optimised Donchian close breakout
ideas.entry: upper = max of the previous (lookback-1) closes, lower = min of the same, both shifted one bar. Signal +1 if close > upper, -1 if close < lower, otherwise keep the previous signal
ideas.exit: Reverse on the opposite break; always in the market after the first signal
ideas.parameters: lookback optimised over 12..168 by profit factor on the training window (best on BTC 2016-2019 hourly was 19). Walk-forward: train 4 years of bars, re-optimise every 30 days of bars. Permutations: 1000 in-sample, 200 walk-forward
ideas.claimed_results: Code comment in donchian.py: best lookback 19, best in-sample profit factor 1.08 (BTC hourly 2016-2019). No p-values are written down anywhere
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: P-0084 100-day breakout (same family; here the lookback is optimised and it is a single market, long/short)
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead: the channel is shifted one bar and the walk-forward optimises only on bars before the fit date. The walk-forward test data ends in 2020 with a 4-year training window, so the out-of-sample stretch is about one year (walkforward_donchian_mcpt.py lines 431-436 in mcpt.txt). Same-bar close fill
ideas.why_priority: The strategy duplicates P-0084; the value is the walk-forward permutation method, listed under frameworks

ideas.name: Swing retracement ratios: do they cluster at 0.618 and 1.618
ideas.entry: Not a trading rule. Directional-change zigzag (a top confirmed when close falls sigma below the running high, a bottom when close rises sigma above the running low), leg ratio = |leg k| / |leg k-1|, kernel density of log(ratio) with bandwidth 0.01, plotted with vertical lines at 0.618 and 1.618
ideas.parameters: sigma 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%; KDE bandwidth 0.01. The result is read by eye; the repo prints no statistic
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead issue because nothing is traded. The claim is unfalsifiable as written: we would need to define a density-mass test around 0.618 and 1.618 and compare it with permuted bars. Sigma needs rescaling for daily bars
ideas.why_priority: Cheap folklore test that tests the premise behind D-10 before we spend time on the harmonic strategy, and it makes a good public result either way

ideas.name: Harmonic XABCD patterns (Gartley, Bat, Butterfly, Crab, Deep Crab, Cypher, Shark)
ideas.entry: Swings from directional_change at sigma. With X, A, B, C the last four confirmed swings and D the current bar's extreme (low if the last swing was a top, high if a bottom, and only if it is the most extreme since the last confirmed swing), compute XA/AB, AB/BC, BC/CD and XA/AD ratios and score them against hard-coded ratio ranges for the seven patterns (log-ratio error, out-of-range punished x2). Enter at the close of bar D when the best pattern error is at or below the threshold: long after a top-to-low leg, short after a bottom-to-high leg. Seven sigma values are run and the signals averaged
ideas.exit: Hold until the next swing is confirmed. No stop and no target
ideas.parameters: sigmas 1%, 1.5%, 2%, 2.5%, 3%, 3.5%, 4%; error threshold 0.5 in main (0.2 in the commented per-sigma tests; swept 0.1..0.75); ratio tables hard-coded. Sigma and threshold swept in-sample
ideas.claimed_results: none (a comment says profit factors above 4 are clipped on the chart because of low sample size)
ideas.red_flags: No strict look-ahead: swings are indexed by their confirmation bar. D is defined from the bar's own low or high, only known at that bar's close, so a fill at that close is optimistic. No stop. The scan stops at the last confirmed swing, so the final segment is dropped (harmonic_patterns.py line 778). Seven patterns x seven sigmas x threshold sweep is a big search space with no out-of-sample; a permutation test must put the whole family inside the loop. Sigma needs rescaling for daily bars
ideas.why_priority: Large untested search space and folklore premise; only worth running if D-09 finds real clustering at the Fibonacci ratios

ideas.name: Head and shoulders / inverse head and shoulders
ideas.entry: Rolling-window swings of half-width 'order' (a swing at bar t-order is confirmed at bar t). Five alternating swings: left shoulder, left armpit, head, right armpit, and a right shoulder defined as the highest close since the right armpit up to the previous bar. Rules: head above both shoulders; each shoulder above the midpoint of the other shoulder and its armpit; shoulder-to-head times within 2.5x of each other. Neckline through the two armpits. Short when close breaks below the neckline (early_find variant: when close falls below the midpoint of the right shoulder and right armpit). The inverse pattern is mirrored for longs
ideas.exit: Two versions coded: (a) hold for head_width bars (right armpit minus left armpit); (b) stop at the right-shoulder price, target = neckline value at entry -/+ head height, time stop at head_width bars, all checked on closes
ideas.parameters: order swept 1..48, early_find on and off; symmetry limit 2.5; no value selected in the code
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found: rw_top and rw_bottom (TechnicalAnalysisAutomation.txt lines 2027-2054) confirm swings late and the code records the confirmation bar. Overlapping patterns and a 48-order x 4-variant sweep in test_hs_patterns.py mean the bar charts are not independent trades. Fills at the close. Pattern counts on daily bars will be small
ideas.why_priority: Classic pattern with fully coded rules, but low prior and a large unpenalised parameter sweep

ideas.name: Flags and pennants breakout
ideas.entry: Pole = move from a confirmed swing to the next opposite swing (rolling-window swings, half-width 'order'). Flag = the consolidation since the pole tip, valid if its width is at most half the pole width and its height is at most 0.75 of the pole height (0.5 in the PIP version). Trendline version: fit support and resistance lines to the flag so far and enter at the close of the first bar that closes beyond the line in the pole's direction (long after up-pole). PIP version: find 5 perceptually important points in the flag and require a zig-zag shape and a breakout beyond the flag line. A pennant is a flag with converging lines
ideas.exit: Hold for flag_width * 1.0 bars after the breakout bar
ideas.parameters: order swept 3..48; hold multiplier 1.0; two detectors (trendline and PIP) selectable
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead found (flag fits use data up to the previous bar and the breakout is tested on the current close). Bugs: the pennant loops in flags_pennants.py use the stale variable flag.conf_x instead of pennant.conf_x (TechnicalAnalysisAutomation.txt lines 591 and 604; test_flag_patterns.py has it right), and lines 391 and 441 project the trendline one bar beyond the current bar. Overlapping patterns, order sweep with no out-of-sample
ideas.why_priority: Fully coded but low prior, a big sweep, and known bugs to fix before use

ideas.name: PIP shape miner with k-means clusters
ideas.markets: BTCUSDT hourly log close, 2018-2019 for the fit; walk-forward version on the full history
ideas.entry: Each bar, take the last 24 log closes, find 5 perceptually important points (vertical-distance method), z-score the 5 PIP prices and assign to the nearest of k k-means centres (k chosen by silhouette search over 5..40). Each cluster's past occurrences are scored by holding 6 bars; the single best cluster by Martin ratio (return over ulcer index) becomes the long cluster and the single worst the short cluster. Trade long when the current window falls in the long cluster, short when it falls in the short cluster
ideas.exit: Hold 6 bars; a new qualifying pattern resets the hold counter (wf_pip_miner.py)
ideas.parameters: n_pips 5, lookback 24, hold 6, clusters 5..40 via silhouette; walk-forward train 2 years of bars, retrain every 1 year
ideas.claimed_results: none (the permutation test that would give a p-value is commented out and 'takes about an hour' per 100 reps)
ideas.red_flags: Cluster selection (best and worst of k clusters, pip_pattern_miner.py lines 1917-1919) is done on the same data it is scored on, so the fit Martin ratio is selection-biased; the repo's own permutation test shuffles log returns and reruns the whole pipeline, which is the right cure. wf_pip_miner.py line 3007: the training slice always starts at bar 1, so the 'rolling' window actually expands. pyclustering needs numpy 1.23.1 (README); sklearn KMeans would replace it. No look-ahead found. Small sample on daily bars, and heavy compute
ideas.why_priority: Data-mined by design, slow, and thin on daily data; only the permutation wrapper is of real value

ideas.name: Permutation entropy as a regime indicator
ideas.entry: unstated (indicator only). Order-3 ordinal patterns over 3 consecutive bars, distribution of the last 168 (6 x 28) patterns, normalised Shannon entropy from 0 to 1, computed for close and for volume
ideas.parameters: order d=3, window multiplier 28 (window = 3! x 28 = 168 patterns)
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead (patterns use the current and two previous bars; the window ends at the current bar). Ties count as >= (line 39). Not a strategy: it would have to be tested as a filter on an existing rule, for example whether RSI(5) dip-buying works better when entropy is low
ideas.why_priority: A plausible filter for the RSI(5) book but needs us to invent the rule, so it is a second-round idea

ideas.name: Hierarchical ATR zigzag swing levels
ideas.entry: unstated (engine only). ATRDirectionalChange: a high is confirmed when a bar's low drops more than ATR below the pending maximum; a low when a bar's high rises more than ATR above the pending minimum. Each swing stores the bar where it occurred and the later bar and close where it was confirmed. HierarchicalExtremes promotes a swing to the next level when it is the extreme of its type flanked by lower (for tops) same-type swings; get_level_high_price(level, lag) and get_level_low_price return the latest confirmed level
ideas.parameters: ATR lookback (1440 in the example), 5 levels in the example
ideas.data_needed_if_not: The author's example is 1-minute BTC; the logic itself runs on daily OHLC
ideas.red_flags: No look-ahead: every swing carries its confirmation index and the sanity checks assert alternation. Fills at the confirmation close are slightly optimistic because the threshold was crossed intrabar. Nothing to test until we write a rule, for example breakout of the latest level-2 high
ideas.why_priority: A clean non-repainting swing engine for later ideas rather than an idea to test in its own right

ideas.name: Moving-average crossover 10/30 long/flat
ideas.entry: Long when SMA(10) of close > SMA(30) of close
ideas.claimed_results: none (profit factor and Sharpe are computed but never printed)
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Kevin Davey golden cross and the 200 vs 222-day MA filter tests
ideas.red_flags: None beyond a same-bar close fill. It is only the demo strategy for the permutation test
ideas.why_priority: Plain MA crossovers are already covered by our golden-cross and MA-filter tests

ideas.name: Decision tree on 6/24/168-bar returns (author's negative control)
ideas.entry: DecisionTreeClassifier(min_samples_leaf=5, random_state=69) on 6, 24 and 168-bar log returns, target = sign of the next 24-bar log return. Long when predicted up, short otherwise
ideas.exit: Reverse on the next prediction flip
ideas.parameters: min_samples_leaf 5; no walk-forward, scored in-sample only
ideas.claimed_results: Author comment: 'This is trash :)'. No numbers
ideas.red_flags: In-sample only by design, so it memorises. NaN predictions in the first 168 bars become -1 shorts (tree_strat.py line 393). Its use is as a known-overfit control for our permutation harness
ideas.why_priority: Not a strategy; use it only to check our harness flags an overfit tree correctly

ideas.name: Visibility-graph random-walk slope forecast
ideas.entry: unstated (function only). network_prediction() builds a transition matrix from the visibility graph, runs a random walk until similarity to the last point converges, and returns a weighted average of the slopes from each earlier point to the last point (Zhan and Xiao 2021, arXiv 2103.13870). No trade rule; the file says it will be covered in a future video
ideas.red_flags: Unfinished and untested in the repo. We would have to invent the trading rule (for example sign of the forecast slope), which makes it our idea rather than his
ideas.why_priority: No rule to test and an unfinished function

frameworks.name: Walk-forward permutation test
frameworks.what_it_is: walkforward_donchian_mcpt.py permutes only the bars after the training window (get_permutation with start_index = train window), then reruns the entire walk-forward, including the re-optimisation at every step, on each permuted series. The real walk-forward profit factor is ranked against 200 permuted ones, p = (1 + count of permuted results at least as good) / n. This tests the whole adaptive procedure out of sample, which the in-sample version cannot
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Apply to any rule with re-fitted parameters (D-01, D-08, anything with a sweep) and to a re-optimised version of the RSI(5) systems. Check that our numba bar_permute port supports start_index and keeps the pre-start bars real

frameworks.name: Joint multi-market permutation
frameworks.what_it_is: get_permutation accepts a list of OHLC frames and applies the same shuffle indices to every market (intrabar high/low/close offsets share one permutation, gaps share another), so cross-market correlation survives. The demo shows BTC/ETH correlation preserved. It asserts identical date indexes
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Needed for the 28-ETF portfolio in P-0084 (shuffling each ETF independently destroys the correlation structure and flatters diversified portfolios) and for pair or relative-strength rules such as D-02. Align the ETF dates first, which means the shortest history sets the sample

frameworks.name: Meta-labelling with purged walk-forward
frameworks.what_it_is: A primary rule generates trades with ATR take-profit, stop and time exit. A random forest (1000 trees, depth 3) is trained on past trades only (entered and exited before the fit date), refitted yearly, and a new trade is taken only if its predicted win probability exceeds 0.5. Compared with taking every trade and with buy and hold. Features are all ATR-normalised so they pool across assets
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Meta-label the RSI(5) dip-buying signals across the nine index ETFs (features: distance below the 200-day MA, ATR-normalised drop, volume ratio, prior-day return). Needs enough trades per training window, so pool markets. Needs its own permutation test, which the repo lacks

frameworks.name: Confirmation-index convention for swings
frameworks.what_it_is: Every swing high or low is stored with two indices: the bar where it occurred and the later bar where it became knowable (conf_index and the close at that bar). rw_top and directional_change do the same in TechnicalAnalysisAutomation. The sanity-check function asserts alternation and monotone indices
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Copy the convention into any pattern idea so entries use only confirmed swings and the look-ahead audit is mechanical

frameworks.name: Whole-pipeline permutation for clustering strategies
frameworks.what_it_is: pip_pattern_miner.py shuffles the close's log returns and reruns the entire fit (pattern extraction, silhouette k search, k-means, best and worst cluster selection) on each permutation, using the Martin ratio (return divided by ulcer index, sign-agnostic) as the score
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Template for testing any strategy whose parameters or clusters are chosen by search: the permutation loop must repeat the search, not just the final rule
